_readme: The payload budget (GUIDELINES §2.5). `ceiling` is a HARD gate on the
built bundle's gzip bytes — tools/payload.mjs --check fails when the
build crosses it, and the suite runs that check on every verify.
Raising a ceiling is a DECISION: edit the number in the same commit
as the change that needs it, and say why in that commit's message.
`history` is the per-release record — append with
`node tools/payload.mjs --record vX.Y.Z` at tag time. Raw bytes are
recorded for parse-cost context; the ceiling is gzip because the wire
is what a first paint waits on.
RAISED TO 99000 IN ITEM 40 SLICE 6 (from 98300), for a teardown that did
not exist: CONTAINER_TEARDOWN.sidepane was `() => {}`, so switching the
side pane off left our head in the document while remount_chrome had
already released its ownership token. The 399 bytes are five unmount
functions, the parts table both directions read, and one deduped observer
replacing two-per-remount. The prose that would have cost another 981 went
to _sidebar.scss, which Sass strips. Slices 7-8 are expected to return it:
if Frappe v16 nests sections, the wrapping surgery deletes ~45 lines.
AND TO 100850 for slice 8b, the Shortcuts region — the survey's verdict was
that people navigate to RECORDS, not pages, and this is 'the single
highest-value addition' for an ERP: pins + recents merged (Stripe's model),
server-side caps (25/15, Dynamics' numbers), render-time permission
re-resolution so a revoked pin vanishes rather than 403ing, and the pin
gesture in the Place row's menu. ~1240 gzip after prose was trimmed.
AND css 21500 -> 22100 / js (after 8d's 102600) -> 105600 for slice 8c,
the account band and panel: the pane's foot becomes ONE toolbar of
cells (canonical order guarded against the registry, corner-pinned
account, rail column flip, density-coupled 36/32px cells), and the
avatar's menu becomes a role=dialog panel — identity with bdi
isolation, instant light/dark/auto through Frappe's own endpoint, the
company sub-list through the vendor's session-defaults write, shortcut
hints, motion on tokens. The dead menu-header branch and styles came
out with it; prose lives in the stylesheets, which Sass strips.
AND css -> 22300 closing item 40's last filed defect: the brand pane's
Glass rebuilds its gradient with the transparency mixed into each stop,
because a gradient cannot go through color-mix() and the pane was
rendering Glass and Blurred Glass identically to Solid.
AND js -> 105700 for slice 9: the end anchor asks last-IN-FLOW instead
of last-child (defect 20), data-bnd-sidepane gains its setter, and the
place row and rail button carry their parts. ~46 gzip of identity and
repair.
AND -> 105760 for slice 11: the rail claims the page-title hamburger
(bnd_own panetoggle, stamped only after the trigger wiring is live).
Plus the narrow stand-down the drawer-safety arm forced: at phone width
the hamburger is the drawer's only opener, and the claim was hiding it.
AND -> 105980 for slice 12: the pane becomes a navigation landmark named
by the place (one writer with the head label), and the vendor's section
disclosure state is mirrored into aria-expanded.
AND -> 106500 for slice 13, the user's two picks: the badge roll-up (a
collapsed section's hidden counts sum into one chip on its header,
derived from the rows - no second fetch) and collapse-all in the Place
row's switcher, every fold through the vendor's own toggle.
AND TO 102600 for slice 8d, drag-to-resize — the survey's clearest
differentiator (every product tool has it, no ERP surveyed does, and
Frappe's own .sidebar-resize-handle never resized anything): the pointer
engine with its 4px latch, the APG splitter keyboard contract, the
zero-network stop menu that WCAG 2.5.7 conformance DEPENDS on, and the
readout chip. ~1660 gzip of designed feature; the argument lives in
_sidebar.scss, the JS carries pointers.
RAISED AGAIN TO 99450 for slice 8: the in-pane filter (the survey's clearest
gap — 6/13 product tools have one, 0/14 ERPs — and ERPs are the ones with
70-link workspaces), the automatic overflow fade replacing the deleted
scroll_fades preference, and aria-current on the pane's active row. ~290
gzip bytes of designed feature after the prose was already trimmed to
pointers; the argument lives in _sidebar.scss, which Sass strips.
98800 was the first number and it was nine bytes too tight: the retry that
mounts the head has to RE-CHECK ITS OWN PREMISE, because it outlives the
call that scheduled it and a pending attempt otherwise lands after the
teardown. That is a correctness line, not a comment, so the ceiling moved
rather than the code.
Ceilings start at ~15% over the v0.12.0 measurement — headroom for a
normal slice, tight enough that a dependency or a generated blob
cannot slip in unnoticed.
SEPARATE CEILINGS, NOT A SUM (item 32; count-free since item 35 — the count drifted twice). `css_gzip` is the desk bundle, which
only an authenticated desk fetches; `web_css_gzip` is bunood-web.<hash>.css,
which every WEBSITE page fetches. They are never both on one page, so summing
them would bound a number nobody pays — and would break every history row's
comparability at the release that introduced the second sheet. Rows before
v0.32.0 carry no web_css_* keys because the file did not exist; that is the
honest shape, not a gap.
THAT SECOND SENTENCE USED TO READ 'the login sheet, which only a logged-out
visitor fetches', and item 33 made it false in the same release that made it
matter: the sheet now loads on every public page, every portal page and every
web form, for signed-in and signed-out visitors alike. The audience for these
bytes went from two routes to the whole website, so the ceiling is now the
tightest one here in practice even though it is the smallest number.
RAISED 98200 -> 98300 by item 40's ownership repair (2026-08-30). The repair is
~40 gzip bytes of runtime: `claim_panehead`, one entry in remount_chrome's
disown list, and a build-only branch in sb_mount_brand. It cost more at first
draft -- 449 bytes -- because the ARGUMENT was written at the JS call sites,
and build.mjs copies that file verbatim by policy, so every comment ships. The
prose moved to _layouts.scss, where Sass strips `//` before the wire and where
the ownership contract already lived. What is left is the feature. Item 40's
slice 4 is a deletion slice and is expected to return this and more; if it does
not, this number should come back down rather than stay as headroom.
tools/payload.mjs THROWS on any dist file that matches no bucket, so a
third entry cannot repeat item 32's near-miss of shipping unmeasured.
